summary.title: (Faster) Facial landmark detector with dlib
summary.one_liner: You learn what dlib's 5-point facial landmark model offers over the 68-point model (about 10x smaller and 8-10% faster), how to run it with OpenCV, and why it is unsuitable for drowsiness detection.
keywords: how many points for face alignment
can 5 landmarks compute eye aspect ratio
takeaways: dlib's 5-point model has 2 points per eye and 1 nose point, at 9.2MB versus 99.7MB for the 68-point model.
In the author's tests the 5-point detector was 8-10% faster than the 68-point detector.
The 5-point model works as a drop-in replacement for face alignment, but it lacks enough eye points for eye aspect ratio drowsiness detection.
A Python script using dlib, imutils VideoStream and OpenCV draws the detected face box and landmarks from a webcam feed.
summary.summary: The post introduces dlib's v19.7 5-point facial landmark detector and compares it with the original 68-point model on speed and model size. It explains the trade-offs between Haar cascades, HOG + Linear SVM and deep learning face detectors. A Python walkthrough uses dlib, imutils and OpenCV to detect faces from a video stream and draw the landmarks. The author closes by explaining why the 5-point model suits face alignment but not drowsiness detection, and promotes a paid course and an email-gated source download.
